behaviour_notes: Trusted senders see no change: our own shell pages can still call every channel, and the server page can still call every 'trusted' channel. The same senders as before are refused, but the refusal now happens in the gate before the handler body runs, and two things about it are different. (1) The error text is generic ("This can only be done from Bee Flow's own settings window." or "This is only available to your Bee Flow workspace.") where it used to name the action ("Changing settings can only be done ..."). (2) The desktop log line is now "refused <channel> from <url>" where it used to be "refused <what> from <url>" followed by "<channel> failed: ...". Only callers that were already being refused can see either change: 'other' pages on any channel, and the server page on shell-only channels. A channel with no trust entry now throws when it is registered (at app start), so the app fails closed. That cannot happen today: TypeScript requires every INVOKE key, and all 30 are classified exactly as the handler bodies were (I checked by script).
open_questions: The spec wanted CHANNEL_TRUST to map each channel to only 'shell' | 'trusted', so the table has no room for the action wording, and the gate's refusal text is generic (see behaviour_notes). If the per-action messages are wanted back, the table would need a `what` per channel. The test does not import handlers.ts, because handlers.ts imports `electron` at module level and plain `node --test` cannot load that. Instead it registers every INVOKE channel through `gatedHandle`, the same function handlers.ts uses, against a stub ipcMain, and checks that each channel refuses both an 'other' sender and a null frame without running the body. Nothing at runtime checks that handlers.ts keeps using `gatedHandle`; that rests on code review and the comment in handlers.ts. I left shared/ipc.ts untouched so the preload bundle does not change; trust.ts imports nothing from electron.

It runs in about 2 s, well under 10 s, so it is not on the denylist.

Recorded budgets (`{_comment, _generated, size}`, measured after H5): server 565, agent-hub 68, mobile 2. Each size is the number of files in the largest strongly connected component that has at least 2 files, and 0 means there is no cycle.

The numbers differ from the audit's (server 603 before H5, roughly 541 expected after it; mobile 5) because the measurement is more accurate:
(a) Comments are stripped by a small tokenizer that understands strings, templates and regexes. The audit counted JSDoc text such as `@type {import('./tools')}` and prose like "import it from '@/x'" as imports. That created false cycles, for example cms/mcp blog<->tools and the mobile webpages/notebooks cycles.
(b) Type-only imports are left out: `import type`, `export type`, `import { type A, type B }` and `typeof import()`.
(c) A spread `...require('./x')` now counts. stores/automationStore.js composes this way, and that pushes server up from 533 to 565 compared with a version without spreads.
(d) tsconfig `paths` aliases (`@/`, `@shared/`) are read from each package's tsconfig.json. `./x.js` resolves to `x.ts`, and `?raw` query suffixes are ignored.

Lazy requires, `import()` and template specifiers without `${}` count anywhere in a file. Not scanned: test files (`*.test.*`, `*.spec.*`, `*.testkit.*`), `__tests__/` and `__mocks__/` folders, and `.d.ts` files. Packages are scanned as `<pkg>/src`, or the whole package when it has no src/, the same rule as count-ratchet. Tarjan's algorithm is iterative, so a deep graph cannot overflow the stack.

`--update` only lowers the budget. `--list` prints the cycle count, all cycle sizes and the files of the largest cycle. Usage errors exit 2.

Outside the lane files I made two small doc edits: a bullet in CLAUDE.md under repository plumbing and one paragraph in server/ARCHITECTURE.md under "The rule is enforced".
